name: Nergal-sar-ezer
overview: Nergal-sar-ezer was a male high official known as the Rab-mag, a title denoting a chief or chief officer, mentioned in the book of Jeremiah. His role as a prominent leader is highlighted by this unique attribute, although his tribal affiliation and family background are not recorded in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Nergal-sar-ezer means 'Nergal protect the prince!' indicating a connection to the Mesopotamian deity Nergal, common in Babylonian culture. The title Rab-mag translates as 'high official,' emphasizing his authoritative position. Both the name and title appear in Jeremiah 39:3, providing insight into his status during the events described there.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Nergal-sar-ezer beyond his designation as the Rab-mag. There are no known relatives or tribal connections mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Nergal-sar-ezer is significant in the biblical narrative as a leading Babylonian official involved in the conquest of Jerusalem. His presence as Rab-mag reflects the administrative structure of Babylonian rule over Judah during this critical period. Although details about his actions are limited, his mention underscores the fulfillment of God's judgment upon Jerusalem through foreign powers.
